description: Over thirty years Huiyuan saw the holy forms three times without speaking of it; at the end, rising from samādhi, he saw Amitābha filling space with transformation buddhas in his halo and the two bodhisattvas, and streams of light proclaiming suffering, emptiness, impermanence and no-self; told he would be born in seven days, he also saw deceased companions.
When Shandao recited, a ray of light issued from his mouth at each recitation, ten or a hundred for ten or a hundred recitations (the tradition's account).

With continuous voiced recitation samādhi is attained and the Buddha and holy assembly are seen clearly before one's eyes (Huaigan); 'great recitation sees a great buddha, small recitation a small buddha'.
Hearing the sixteenth contemplation, Vaidehī and her attendants see the vast Land of Bliss, the Buddha and the two bodhisattvas, and she gains the acceptance of non-arising.
At the deathbed the dying may see signs of their sins or the lotus-dais and holy assembly; attendants record them and help repent the former until the latter appear (Shandao).

For the precept-breaker of the lower-middle grade the fires of hell appear at death; on hearing of Amitābha's virtues they turn into a cool wind bearing flowers with transformation buddhas who welcome him.
In meditative absorption Mao Ziyuan awakened on hearing a crow's call: 'twenty years searching on paper ... suddenly hearing the crow I knew I had used my mind wrongly'.
Hōnen's samādhi record tells of visions in nenbutsu samādhi (1198–1206) of the Pure Land's ground, jewel trees, ponds and the Buddha's form, attained without contemplative effort through recitation.
Hōnen dreamt of meeting Shandao, whose lower body was golden, who approved his spreading of the exclusive nenbutsu (the 'meeting of the two patriarchs').
At dawn on the ninety-fifth day of his retreat at the Rokkakudō (1201) Prince Shōtoku / Kannon appeared to Shinran in a dream with a verse, after which he went to Hōnen.
At Kumano Hongū (1274) the deity appeared to Ippen and told him birth was settled for all as Namu Amida Butsu and to give the talismans to all.
In 1117, in samādhi, Amida appeared to Ryōnin and revealed the verse of the interfusing nenbutsu.
Saying the nenbutsu without the dancing joy one expects and without wishing to go quickly to the Pure Land — shared by Shinran and taken as the working of blind passions, for which the vow was made.
Visions arising in the recitation retreat are not to be told lightly; good ones are known to oneself, bad ones repented.
